evidence.text: Large-volume and 1/(at) expansions, Gaussian elimination of H fluctuations, and numerical comparisons of full versus frozen models test vacuum values, auxiliary fields and masses. Numerical examples use a minimal dilaton-plus-one-complex-structure toy sector with leading S₀=U₀=1 and W₀=1.

sources.title: Perturbative Stability along the Supersymmetric Directions of the Landscape

evidence.text: Takagi factorization of the complex symmetric fermion mass matrix; projection of the scalar Hessian along fermion eigenvectors orthogonal to the sGoldstino; first-order eigenvalue perturbation theory for small mixing between sectors.

sources.title: A comment on effective field theories of flux vacua

evidence.text: Uses Kähler potentials, superpotentials and Kähler-covariant vacuum equations to exhibit no-scale cancellation, condensate stabilization and scale separation. The IIB discussion estimates the displacement of a stabilized volume modulus after adding supersymmetry-breaking energy.

sources.title: On the Effective Description of Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Superconformal component formalism retains auxiliary fields while solving the H scalar and auxiliary equations simultaneously. Substitution into the original Lagrangian is compared with simply freezing H at leading F-flat values; power counting estimates the omitted terms.

sources.title: Perturbative Stability along the Supersymmetric Directions of the Landscape

evidence.text: Altland–Zirnbauer CI ensembles model fermion masses. Marčenko–Pastur densities are transformed into scalar spectra; the Wishart correspondence, Tracy–Widom tails and large-deviation formulas estimate atypical spectra.

sources.title: A comment on effective field theories of flux vacua

evidence.text: Reviews Wilsonian reasoning: integrate out dynamics above the low-energy cutoff, including strongly coupled nonperturbative sectors. Organizing solely by perturbative coupling order is insufficient; the resulting low-energy vacuum must be determined self-consistently.

sources.title: Six and seven dimensional extrema of Non-SUSY heterotic theory with non-maximal enhancements

evidence.text: Can right-moving lattice symmetries systematically generate non-maximally enhanced extrema of the non-supersymmetric heterotic one-loop potential, and what do their Hessians imply for perturbative stability and refined de Sitter bounds?

sources.title: Minimal Stability in Maximal Supergravity

evidence.text: Across maximal gauged supergravities, what necessary conditions permit perturbative scalar stability when supersymmetry is broken, and can non-maximally-supersymmetric critical points approach the maximally supersymmetric vacuum continuously?

sources.title: The de Sitter swampland conjecture and supersymmetric AdS vacua

evidence.text: Does weak-coupling positivity create the same obstruction to supersymmetric heterotic dilaton stabilization that the note identifies in one-modulus IIB models?

sources.title: Metastable spontaneous breaking of N=2 supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can rigid N=2 supersymmetry break spontaneously in metastable vacua without constant Fayet–Iliopoulos terms, using only one hypermultiplet and one Abelian vector multiplet? What scalar-mass bounds follow, and what can be inferred about an extension to de Sitter supergravity?

sources.title: Constraints on meta-stable de Sitter flux vacua

evidence.text: Can geometry-independent stability constraints exclude metastable de Sitter flux critical points when supersymmetry breaking is dominated by the axion-dilaton, and what restrictions follow for nonsupersymmetric AdS vacua and vacuum statistics?

sources.title: Universal dS vacua in STU-models

evidence.text: Can polynomial superpotentials with generalized fluxes yield analytically controlled stable de Sitter critical points near supersymmetric or no-scale Minkowski points, and reproduce the local vacuum properties obtained using nonperturbative superpotentials?

sources.title: Smooth String Vacua in a Gravitationally Nonperturbative Regime

evidence.text: Construct the Kähler-invariant combination Geff=K5d+log|W5d,eff|² using SL(2,Z) invariance, Dedekind η and the invariant j-function, matching Geff→−log(T+T̄)+log n² at large T. Insert the corrected potential into the BPS flow; large-Re T corrections are interpreted as M5 instantons with action 2πT.

sources.title: Lectures on Supersymmetry Breaking

evidence.text: Use holomorphy, symmetry charges assigned to background couplings, instantons, gaugino condensation and electric-magnetic duality to constrain SQCD dynamics. Legendre transforms with respect to sources generate useful 1PI superpotentials, whose interpretation must be distinguished from a Wilsonian action.

sources.title: Naturalness versus supersymmetric nonrenormalization theorems

evidence.text: Promote superpotential couplings to background chiral fields. Combine selection rules under the enlarged symmetry group with local holomorphy, smooth weak-gauge-coupling behavior, and calculable limits as superpotential couplings vanish.

sources.title: Exact results on the space of vacua of four-dimensional SUSY gauge theories

evidence.text: Holomorphy of chiral expectation values and superpotentials, combined with global-symmetry selection rules, constrains exact dependence on masses and the dynamical scale.

sources.title: Nonrenormalization theorems in nonrenormalizable theories

evidence.text: Test supersymmetric vacua by eliminating terms linear in constant auxiliary fields F_n and D_A. Gauge invariance extends a stationary superpotential configuration along a complexified gauge orbit; a stationary effective Kähler potential on that orbit also satisfies the D-term condition.

sources.title: Smooth String Vacua in a Gravitationally Nonperturbative Regime

evidence.text: Use the warped metric ds5²=e^(2a)ημνdxμdxν+e^(8a)dy² and first-order supersymmetric flow equations for a(y) and T(y). Classically, boundary delta-function sources produce a linear harmonic function H(y), with Re T proportional to H³.
